subject: Pricing follow-up: batching & concurrency assumptions for BrightHealth pilot
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Sonia Patel <sonia@brighthealth.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing follow-up: batching & concurrency assumptions for BrightHealth pilot

Hi Sonia — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can put together an accurate pricing model: 

Summary notes from discovery:
- Pilot scope: conversational triage assistant for member intake (chat + short system prompts).
- Expected pilot volume: starts small (approx 5M tokens/mo) and scales to a steady state between 50M–200M tokens/mo depending on feature rollout.
- Typical request size: median ~400 tokens (prompt + response), tail up to ~2k tokens for long threads.
- Concurrency & pattern: weekday business-hours heavy, estimated peak concurrent active sessions ~50–80. Baseline/overnight lower.
- SLAs: soft latency target for UX; initial tolerance for batching as long as first-byte latency for streaming responses remains reasonable.

Specific asks for pricing model (can you confirm):
1) Target $/1M tokens you expect (ballpark) for the pilot and for an annualized committed price?
2) Of the token volume, what percent do you expect to be short (<128 tokens) vs medium (128–512) vs long (>512)?
3) Do you expect continuous traffic throughout the day (steady) or concentrated spikes (e.g., 10–2pm PST)?
4) Any compliance/retention constraints that affect caching or prefix reuse?

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll put together a pricing estimate using a few unit-economics scenarios (continuous batching vs more conservative batching; reserved capacity assumptions).
- Loop Aditya (SE) for a 30–45m technical deep-dive to validate concurrency/batching assumptions and run a quick perf profile if you’re open to it.
- If numbers look good, we’ll send a short SOW draft and a HubSpot quote.

I’ve attached a preliminary pricing worksheet (redwood-pricing-estimate.xlsx) with the fields I’ll populate once you confirm the items above. Would love to get your answers by end of day Thursday so we can push an estimate next week.

Thanks — Camila

From: Sonia Patel <sonia@brighthealth.ai>

Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up: batching & concurrency assumptions for BrightHealth pilot

Hi Camila — thanks for the recap, that’s accurate. Answers below and a few additional notes from our side: 

1) Target $/1M tokens: for pilot we have a soft internal target around $7–9 per 1M tokens. For a committed annual price we’d expect better — ideally in the $5–7 per 1M tokens range if we commit to >500M tokens/yr.

2) Token size distribution (estimated):
- Short (<128): 25% (quick intents and confirmations)
- Medium (128–512): 55% (typical triage Q&A)
- Long (>512): 20% (member history + longer follow-ups)

3) Traffic pattern:
- We see a pronounced daytime peak M–F (~9:00–15:00 local). Roughly 60% of daily traffic in that window with short spikes around 11:30 and 14:30.
- We expect traffic to be fairly continuous during peak hours (not all-in bursts, more like a steady high-concurrency tail).

4) Compliance:
- PHI allowed but must be encrypted at rest and in transit; retention policy is 90 days in the service initially. Caching of PII/PHI should be opt-in and masked; prefix caching is fine for non-sensitive content.

Concurrency and batching notes:
- We’re assuming up to ~60 concurrent active sessions initially; scale to 100+ with broader rollout.
- Continuous batching is acceptable — we prefer batching strategies that preserve streaming-first-byte behavior. Our UI streams tokens to the client; latency for the first stream packet should remain below ~250ms for a good UX.

We’ll attach an example usage export for April (tokens per hour) after I get permission from our analytics team — will send separately.

Cheers,
Sonia
Sonia Patel | Director, Product Platform
BrightHealth
sonia@brighthealth.ai
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-05-15T11:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up: batching & concurrency assumptions for BrightHealth pilot

Thanks Sonia — that’s super helpful and exactly what we needed. A few clarifying points so we size and price correctly: 

- Confirming the distribution: short 25% / medium 55% / long 20% — we’ll model that.
- For continuous batching: we’ll assume steady batching windows with opportunistic prefix caching for non-PHI content. We’ll avoid caching anything flagged as PHI by default.
- For first-byte streaming latency target: we’ll design the perf profile to keep initial-frame latency <= 250ms under expected peak concurrency (60–100). That will inform whether reserved capacity is required vs. pay-as-you-go.

I’m attaching the preliminary pricing worksheet with two baseline scenarios: 
A) Continuous batching optimized: assumes 60–80% batching efficiency across payloads and a target unit price near $6.50 per 1M tokens for pilot volumes.
B) Conservative (lower batching): assumes ~30–40% batching efficiency and higher unit cost ~ $9.50 per 1M tokens.

Proposed next steps: 
- Schedule a 30–45m technical deep-dive with Aditya to validate concurrency and test a small perf profile (we can run a rapid job against a sandbox model to measure first-byte streaming under batching).
- If you’re comfortable, we’ll draft the SOW and a HubSpot quote using scenario A as the baseline and note the fallback pricing in scenario B.

When are you available for the deep-dive? We have slots tomorrow 10:00–11:00am PT or Thursday 2:00–3:00pm PT.

Best — Camila
